reason: Safe and well aimed. The Achilles pain got sharper during Thursday's tempo, and the draft treats that as the main issue. It drops all quality work, asks for a sports physio or doctor to see it this week (ideally before Thursday), flags red-flag symptoms, and cuts the week to about 25 mi from 31. All runs are flat easy miles with heart-rate caps, and the long run is held at 8 mi. That respects the fixed Monday and Friday rest days and Johnny's preference for cautious loading. Each day can be run as written. The one weakness is the answers. Both questions are mostly handed off to the physio. The plan does show Johnny he can keep running easy, but answer (1) doesn't say so directly. Answer (2) could have spelled out warning signs to stop for, such as pain that gets worse during a run, a limp, swelling or morning stiffness that keeps getting worse, instead of "I cannot tell you." Being honest about the limits is right, but the anxious athlete gets less reassurance and direction than he could. With the race on 15 November, it would also have helped to say how this affects the goal.
